description:
Separate calls: every `run` is a fresh shell, and only the working directory crosses calls.

Each script is split at `#--call--` lines into separate calls. Our shell's example starts each call
in the directory the previous one ended in, as a caller passing back the returned `cwd` does; the
oracle runs each call as its own `bash -c` in the directory the marker names (`/` when it names
none). Anything else a script wants to keep, it writes to a file.

cases.name: calls: the working directory carries
cases.script:
mkdir -p /tmp/w && cd /tmp/w
#--call-- /tmp/w
pwd; cd ..; pwd
#--call-- /tmp
pwd

cases.name: calls: relative paths resolve from the carried directory
cases.script:
mkdir -p /tmp/r/sub; cd /tmp/r; echo data > sub/f
#--call-- /tmp/r
cat sub/f; cd sub
#--call-- /tmp/r/sub
cat f; echo "$PWD"

cases.name: calls: exit keeps the directory it left in
calls: variables and exports end with their call
cases.script:
x=1; export y=2; declare -i n=5
#--call--
echo "[${x-unset}] [${y-unset}] [${n-unset}]"

cases.name: calls: arrays end with their call
calls: functions end with their call
calls: aliases end with their call
cases.script:
shopt -s expand_aliases; alias ll='echo listing'
#--call--
alias; echo done

cases.name: calls: shell options end with their call
cases.script:
set -eu; set -o pipefail; shopt -s nullglob
#--call--
set -o | grep -E '^(errexit|nounset|pipefail)'; shopt nullglob

cases.name: calls: the last status does not carry
calls: traps end with their call
cases.script:
trap 'echo err' ERR; trap '' PIPE; trap 'echo bye' EXIT
#--call--
trap -p; false; echo after

cases.name: calls: readonly ends with its call
calls: positional parameters and the directory stack end with their call
cases.script:
set -- a b c; cd /tmp; mkdir -p s; pushd s >/dev/null
#--call-- /tmp/s
echo $#; dirs

cases.name: calls: each call is a new process
calls: settings kept in a file
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'x=kept' 'greet() { echo "hi $1"; }' 'set -o pipefail' > /tmp/env.sh
#--call--
. /tmp/env.sh; echo $x; greet you; set -o | grep pipefail
